main.title: Solving "too large to make" through large-format printing.
main.copy: Large-format additive manufacturing (WAAM/LFAM) is going commercial in Europe. We connect large-scale metal and polymer 3D printing to real problems on Japan's factory floor.

main.title: Large-format metal and polymer printing
main.copy: Turnkey systems with build volumes from 2x1m to 3x2m are now commercially available replacing work once written off as "too small a lot to tool up for" or "too large to machine." No tooling means the economics work from a single unit.

main.title: Where it is already ahead overseas
main.note: Overseas cases are based on manufacturer-published materials and do not represent our own track record.

main.copy: The common thread -- one-off large high-mix -- is exactly what conventional processes handle worst.

main.title: All the numbers up front
main.copy: Entry-level turnkey systems run roughly EUR400000-450000 with a standard lead time of 18-24 weeks after firm order (manufacturer-provided figures). Japan's labor-saving investment subsidy catalog has included 3D printers since October 2025 adding tailwind to the investment case. At this scale of investment careful screening before ordering has real value.

main.title: We judge fit before you commit
main.copy: We screen against four conditions -- part size lot volume material and current process cost/lead time -- to judge whether large-format printing will actually help. Telling you it is not a fit when it is not is part of the job.

main.title: Your guide not a seller
main.copy: We are not an exclusive agent for any single manufacturer. We work non-exclusively case by case to bridge you to European manufacturers -- building a project brief from your requirements and connecting you directly with the manufacturer's team designed alongside Japan's existing machining grinding heat-treatment and inspection network.

main.title: Tell us about your process -- 30 minutes no charge
main.copy: A free 30-minute hearing on your target process. If there is potential a paid on-site diagnosis (quoted individually) delivers candidate processes rough impact estimates and a manufacturer-ready brief.
